dedupe_keys.name: low frequency triboelectric energy harvester tests for bridge sensors

description: Université Gustave Eiffel researchers tested triboelectric nanogenerators as possible power sources for wireless structural-health sensors. The Data in Brief article describes a custom low-frequency sinusoidal motion platform intended to resemble bridge-cable vibration. The team measured output voltage under several resistor loads and capacitor charging times, then calculated current, power and energy per cycle. Zenodo lists public raw and processed ZIP archives plus three instrument-specification PDFs under CC BY 4.0. Its named landing and API opened, but the archive contents and the home-developed calculation script were not inspected. Coverage is limited to controlled bench tests in Nantes, France, not measurements from an operating bridge or proof that a sensor can run unattended. Motion waveform, harvester geometry and electrical load limit transfer to other structures; ageing in service was not measured. A reviewer-assessed use is bounding harvested-power assumptions in simulated wireless bridge-monitoring networks. data-bangkok-37-storey-building-vibration-2025-earthquake is a related structural-vibration observation record, but the excitation and instruments were not compared. No ZIP, device PDF or article PDF was downloaded.
